answer: Because the vine stake is held until the inlet settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the grove audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 6% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A farm running 195 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
